how.title: How it works
how.encrypted: Everything private is encrypted in your browser before it leaves it. Relays and media servers store it without being able to read it.
how.account: An account is your key, encrypted with your password and published under an address only your username and password can produce. Nobody can find, spam or overwrite it, and a wrong password simply finds nothing. The key itself works in other nostr apps too.
how.settings: Your settings, friends and block list are encrypted to your own key and follow you to every device you sign in on.
how.relays: Everything travels as signed nostr events over relays: servers anyone can run, and you choose which. Relays can drop old data, so each device keeps what it has seen and sends its copy back when a relay reconnects. The newest version always wins.
how.offline: Changes made offline are kept on this device and sent when a relay is reachable again.
how.media: Photos are scaled down and stripped of what cameras store in them, such as the location, then encrypted before they go to a media server. Every photo is checked against its fingerprint when it opens, so no server can swap it. If none of your servers takes encrypted files, you are asked before a photo goes up unencrypted.
how.backup: Backups hold your key and every signed event, so a backup restores everything — even your account — when no relay and no other device has it any more.
how.linkKeys: Links that open something private carry its key after the #, the part browsers never send to any server. A link is a key: whoever has it can pass it on, and it can’t be taken back.
how.direct: A room is named and encrypted by the secret in its link. Data goes straight between the browsers when it can, and through a relay when it can’t, encrypted end to end either way.
how.signed: Public posts are signed nostr events. Everyone sees the same thing, and nobody can change your posts or post in your name.
how.pow: Posting takes proof of work: a few seconds of computing for a person, hours for a flood. Posts without it are not shown.
how.expiry: Posts carry an end date. When it passes, relays drop them and apps stop showing them.
how.friends: Friends are mutual: one asks, the other accepts. Requests and what you share with friends travel sealed, so relays see neither what it is nor who sent it.
how.blocks: Blocking someone hides them in every app, on all your devices. Your block list is encrypted, so nobody sees whom you blocked. Reports are public and signed, for relay operators and other people.
how.privateMessages: Private messages are sealed and wrapped for the one person they are for. Relays see neither what you write nor who sent it.

account.devicesText: Every device signed in with this key, as far as they have reported in. Signing one out forgets the key there the next time it connects; a device that never connects again keeps the key, which is what a new password is for.

account.signOutOthersDone: The other devices sign out when they next connect.
how.spaces: Every board, feed or market here serves one space: a named community with rules, moderators and, when it has them, relays of its own. Posts name their space, so one space’s posts never mix with another’s, and two hubs that name the same space share it.
how.audiences: Posts for friends or a circle are sealed with a key only its members are given, each in a sealed note. When someone leaves (you unfriend or block them, or take them out of the circle), the next posts use a new key they never get; what they could read before stays readable to them. “Only me” uses a key no one else is ever given.

gate.account.text: An account is a username and a password for your key, so it comes with you to every device you sign in on. No email, no phone number, nothing about you but the name you choose. It takes a moment in the settings, and then you come back here.
gate.account.keyText: You use a key without an account. Give it a username and a password in the settings (creating an account keeps your key), and then you come back here.
